name: skipped: exact prefix match
spec_quote: "Leland" skips "Leland Inc" and "leland"; it does not skip "Cleland"

name: skipped: case-insensitive prefix match
spec_quote: True when the company name, trimmed and lower-cased, STARTS WITH any of the names (each trimmed and lower-cased; empty names ignored).

name: skipped: no prefix match inside a word
spec_quote: it does not skip "Cleland" (no prefix match inside a word start other than the beginning).

name: skipped: missing company
spec_quote: False for an empty / missing company, or when names is empty / None.

name: skipped: empty names list
spec_quote: False for an empty / missing company, or when names is empty / None.

name: skipped: trims both sides and ignores empty name
spec_quote: True when the company name, trimmed and lower-cased, STARTS WITH any of the names (each trimmed and lower-cased; empty names ignored).

name: pending: dict without sheet name, unanswered question waits, answered one does not

questions.question: Why do you want this job?

Referrals: Why do you want this job?

spec_quote: handled is a dict {name: set-or-list of question TEXTS, or None}: name missing → every unanswered question waits

name: pending: dict value None means nothing waits

questions.question: Why do you want this job?

spec_quote: value None → nothing waits

name: pending: dict texts exclude only the listed question texts
spec_quote: otherwise a question waits only when its "question" text is NOT in that collection.

name: pending: handled as list of sheet names
spec_quote: handled is a list / set / None of sheet NAMES: when the sheet's name is in it, nothing waits

name: pending: derived answer accepted, but not when risk present or kind high_risk

questions.question: Do you have the right to work?

spec_quote: when sheet.accept_derived is true and the question has block "derived", no risk, kind != "high_risk" and a truthy "suggested".

name: pending: sheet without a name yields no ids
spec_quote: Not a dict sheet, or no / empty name → [].

name: pending: handled None waits on every unanswered question in sheet order
spec_quote: otherwise every unanswered question waits.

name: languages: multi-select list joins picks in profile order

field.label: Which languages do you speak fluently?

spec_quote: when the field type is multi / checkbox, or the label contains "languages" (plural), "all that apply", "select all", "check all" or "fluency": the answer is all picks joined by " | " (e.g. "Spanish | English").

name: languages: radio but plural label counts as multi
spec_quote: when the field type is multi / checkbox, or the label contains "languages" (plural) ... the answer is all picks joined by " | ".

name: languages: first / mother tongue asks for the single native language

field.label: What is your first language / mother tongue?

spec_quote: If the label says native / first / mother / primary: a single answer, the native language's option.

name: languages: Spanish level picks Native

field.label: What is your level of Spanish?

spec_quote: It names a profile language → the first option ... matching, in order: native → native|mother tongue, C2, bilingual, fluent, expert, advanced

name: languages: English professional level picks professional working
spec_quote: professional → "full professional" or "professional working", professional, fluent, C1, advanced or expert.

name: languages: German level maps to None option
spec_quote: It names another language → the option that starts with none / no proficiency / not applicable / n/a / I do not speak / no knowledge / no experience / not proficient

name: languages: German level with no none option stays unknown
spec_quote: no such option → unknown, ask = true (never claim a level in a language the candidate does not speak).

name: languages: unnamed CEFR level asks per job
spec_quote: The label names no language (e.g. "CEFR Level") → status unknown with ask = true (asked per job, not answered).

name: languages: programming languages are not language questions

field.label: Which programming languages are you proficient in?

spec_quote: Not language questions (no answer from this rule): labels about programming / coding / code / software / scripting / query language / frameworks.

name: languages: query language is not a language question

field.label: Which query language do you use most?

spec_quote: Not language questions (no answer from this rule): labels about programming / coding / code / software / scripting / query language / frameworks.

name: no-answer: single negative statement in a statement list

field.label: Have you previously been employed at Affirm?
options: I have been employed at Affirm as a full-time employee
I have not previously been employed at Affirm
I have been employed at Affirm as an intern

expect_value: I have not previously been employed at Affirm
spec_quote: pick the option when EXACTLY ONE option starts with a negative statement ... Example: options "I have not previously been employed at Affirm" ... → the first.

name: no-answer: two negative statements leave it unknown

field.label: Have you ever worked at Acme?
options: I have not worked at Acme
I have never worked at Acme
I have worked at Acme as an intern

spec_quote: Two or more negative statements, or none → no answer (unknown).

name: no-answer: no negative statement leaves it unknown

field.label: Have you previously been employed at Globex?
options: I worked at Globex as an intern
I worked at Globex as a contractor

spec_quote: Two or more negative statements, or none → no answer (unknown).

name: languages: options starting with level codes are not a language list
spec_quote: A LIST of languages: the label contains "language" or "languages" and at least two options name a language, and no option starts with a level code (A1..C2, L1..L3).

name: languages: native language not among options → no pick, unknown
spec_quote: For each profile language (in profile order) pick the option that starts with it, else the first option that contains it. ... No pick → no answer from this rule.

name: languages: certification options are ignored when matching a level
spec_quote: It names a profile language → the first option (ignoring options that mention a certification) matching, in order: native → native|mother tongue, C2, bilingual, fluent, expert, advanced

name: languages: list where only one profile language has an option
spec_quote: For each profile language (in profile order) pick the option that starts with it, else the first option that contains it. ... the answer is all picks joined by " | "
